I suppose the title seems like a bit of a paradox. How can Chaotic Evil actually be Lawful Good?

Take this group from one of my campaigns: The Acolytes of Gloom. They believe that to experience happiness in the eternal afterlife, a person must experience suffering in their mortal life. They want everyone to be happy in the afterlife, so they steal from them, beat them, torture them, etc.

However, because death is an escape from suffering, they never kill anyone, even in self defence. They are willing to die, ending their suffering in this world and possibly preventing eternal happiness, rather than kill someone and do the same to them. They care more about others than they do about themselves.

At first glance, a group of maniacs who try to make life terrible for everyone just for the sake of making life terrible would seem like Chaotic Evil. I would argue that they are Lawful Good. They are willing to sacrifice themselves for the good of others, always sticking to their principles.

I think the long-standing paradigm of Good and Evil is a bit inadequate for discussing alignment. Two opposites may both be doing what they believe is good and righteous and think the other to be evil. I'd define good as willing to put the needs of others before your own and evil being the opposite- putting your own needs before those of others. Neutral, of course, would be in the middle.
Alignments- Chaotic Evil may actually be Lawful Good
